author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: The fossil fuel age
summary: Global energy data going back to 1800 show how slowly energy sources change. Energy production, mainly the burning of fossil fuels, accounts for around three-quarters of global greenhouse gas emissions. NOAA says carbon dioxide is rising mostly because of fossil fuels burned for energy, and atmospheric carbon dioxide is now 50 percent higher than before the Industrial Revolution.

uncertainty.note: Transition accelerated from the late eighteenth century with coal-powered steam engines and continues into the twenty-first century.

as_recorded.value: since the start of the Industrial Revolution

where.modern_name: No single place; stand-in pin at Coalbrookdale, England
where.historical_name: Coalbrookdale, Shropshire, Kingdom of Great Britain

importance.justification: The transition from organic energy to fossil fuels unlocked unprecedented mechanical power, reshaping global civilization and altering Earth's atmosphere.

related.because: Mechanization and steam engine deployment during the Industrial Revolution catalyzed the transition to coal and other fossil fuels.
Combustion of coal, oil, and gas released ancient carbon that accumulated in the atmosphere and drove global warming.

sources.title: Energy Mix
sources.author: Hannah Ritchie, Pablo Rosado and Max Roser

reviewer_note: There is no agreed start date; 1800 is where the energy data begins. The pin at Coalbrookdale in England is a stand-in, not a place the sources name.
